label: copy phase: input k while outputting b (recalling a "k b" bigram), late in the copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original phase or on the delimiter step. Nearly all activation mass (92%) is on steps where the input is k, and 89% is on steps where the output is b. So the feature fires when the model has just re-emitted k and must now output the b that followed it in the original sequence (the original bigram k b). It needs recall_idx >= 3: it is silent at recall_idx 0-1 and weak at 2. The strongest examples are k b b endings late in long sequences. Weaker, low-mass activity (about 20% of mass): input b followed by b (b b), input k followed by some other token with b coming next, and occasional k k b. Silent on all other tokens. Dev: precision 0.88, recall 0.59, F1 0.71, mass recall 0.80. Recall is lost mostly on low-activation k/b-related steps.

issues: All factual claims hold up on the dev profile. Activation occurs only in the copy phase (100% of mass, none in the original phase or on <DEL>). in_tok k carries 91.6% of mass, in_tok b 8.4% and every other input 0. out_tok b carries 89.0%. By recall_idx: 0 at 0-1, 1.5% at 2, and lift of 2.7-4.3x at 3 and above.
The recall_idx >= 3 cut is justified. k->b at recall_idx 1 has precision 0.0 over 562 steps, and at recall_idx 2 it is 0.11. Without the cut, k->b precision drops to 0.58.
The 'k b b is strongest' claim checks out. k->b with next_out b has precision 1.0, and its mass share (4.5%) is about three times its count share (1.6%). The class is small (45 test steps).

Remaining false positives (10%) cluster where many outputs are still left: with to_go >= 3, precision is 0.73 (572 dev steps); with to_go <= 2 it is 0.95. Tightening to to_go <= 3 lowers F1 (0.67), so the original predicate is the better trade-off.

The misses are systematic but low-activation and low-precision, so no predicate can cover them. b->b at recall_idx >= 3: precision 0.22, mass 8%. k->k: precision 0.09, mass 5%. k followed by b within 1-3 outputs: precision 0.13, mass 7%. Coverage by activation quartile is 0.21/0.49/0.80/0.95, so the misses are mostly low-activation steps.

Count recall is only 0.615 (F1 0.73). The 'explained' verdict rests on precision 0.90 and mass recall 0.82, which the test split confirms. Widening to any k/b input with b output pushes mass recall to 0.88 but drops precision to 0.56 and F1 to 0.64, so the original predicate stays.
